Section 2.  Partial Taking.

If any portion of the Leased Premises, the shared parking areas, or the building is taken such that the remaining square footage is reduced by ten percent (10%) or more, or such that patient access to or parking for the Leased Premises is materially impaired, Tenant may terminate this Lease by written notice to Landlord given within sixty (60) days after Tenant receives notice of the taking. If Tenant does not elect to terminate, this Lease shall continue as to the remaining portion of the Leased Premises, Landlord shall restore the remaining improvements to an architectural whole at Landlord’s expense, and Base Rent and Additional Rent shall be equitably reduced until such restoration is substantially complete.

If a taking permanently reduces the Leased Premises by twenty percent (20%) or more or makes the remainder reasonably unsuitable for the Permitted Use, Tenant may terminate this Lease by written notice given within thirty (30) days after notice of the taking. Landlord may terminate if the taking materially impairs the operation or economic viability of the building. If neither party terminates, this Lease shall continue as to the remainder, Landlord shall restore the base building and shell to an architectural whole, and rent shall be reduced in proportion to the portion permanently taken.

Section 2.  Landlord’s Remedies.

Upon an uncured Event of Default, Landlord may terminate this Lease upon written notice to Tenant and recover actual damages permitted by applicable law, or, without terminating this Lease, re-enter and relet the Leased Premises on Tenant’s behalf and recover from Tenant any deficiency between the rent due under this Lease and the rent actually collected, in each case subject to Landlord’s duty to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate its damages, including by making reasonable efforts to relet the Leased Premises promptly following any termination or repossession.

Upon an Event of Default, Landlord may terminate this Lease, re-enter and relet the Leased Premises without terminating, and recover all damages permitted by law, including rent deficiencies, default interest, attorneys’ fees, and the unamortized cost of tenant improvements, rent abatement, and leasing commissions. Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate damages, but shall not be required to prioritize the Leased Premises over other vacancies, accept below-market terms, or alter the intended use or character of the building. Tenant shall have no right to offset, deduct, counterclaim, or withhold rent.

Delay of Commencement Date.  Landlord shall not be liable for any damage or loss incurred by Tenant for Landlord’s failure or inability, for whatever cause or reason, to deliver possession of the Premises by any particular date (including the Lease Commencement Date), nor shall this Lease be void or voidable on account of such failure or inability to deliver possession of the Premises. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if Landlord does not deliver possession of the Premises to Tenant by the date which is sixty (60) days from the Lease Commencement Date, Tenant shall have the right to terminate this Lease by written notice to Landlord, indicating Tenant’s desire to terminate this Lease (the “Delay Notice”).  Landlord shall have thirty (30) days after Landlord’s receipt of the Delay Notice, to tender possession of the Premises to Tenant, and in the event that Landlord is still unable to deliver possession of the Premises to Tenant within such time, then upon the thirty-first (31st) day after Landlord’s receipt of the Delay Notice (the “Delay Termination Date”), this Lease shall be deemed terminated, and of no further force or effect, with Landlord and Tenant thereafter being relieved of any further obligations to one another under this Lease.  Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Delay Termination Date shall be extended by the number of days that work on the Premises is delayed due to no fault of Landlord, or the   fault, neglect, acts or omissions of Tenant, or due to acts of God, labor disputes, strikes, fires, rainy or stormy weather, acts or failures to act of public agencies, inability to obtain labor or materials, earthquake, war, insurrection, riots and other causes beyond Landlord’s reasonable control.  In the event of any delay in delivery of the Premises to Tenant, the Lease Term shall remain unaffected, and this Lease shall terminate on the Lease Termination Date.

Commencement Date.  Landlord shall deliver the Leased Premises no later than November 1, 2026.  If Landlord fails to do so, Tenant may terminate on ten (10) days’ written notice and recover the Security Deposit and all prepaid amounts in full, and Landlord shall pay Tenant’s documented out-of-pocket architectural, engineering, permitting, and legal costs incurred in reliance on the Lease. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the proposed Termination Date shall be extended by thirty (30) days due to acts of God, labor disputes, strikes, fires, earthquake, war, insurrection, riots and other causes deemed force majeure.  In the event of any delay in delivery of the Premises to Tenant under these circumstances only, the Lease Term shall remain unaffected, and this Lease shall terminate on the Lease Termination Date.
Section 2.  Landlord Cooperation.

Landlord shall reasonably cooperate with Tenant, at no material cost to Landlord, in connection with Tenant’s efforts to obtain and maintain such licenses and approvals, including by providing documentation regarding the building’s construction, systems, and compliance history reasonably requested by a licensing authority, and by promptly executing any landlord consent or acknowledgment reasonably required by such authority.

At Tenant’s cost, Landlord shall reasonably cooperate by providing existing building documentation, executing customary landlord consents and acknowledgments, and providing reasonable access for inspections, in each case at no material cost or liability to Landlord. Landlord shall not be required to modify the building, incur third-party expense, make any healthcare-specific representation, or join Tenant’s regulatory filing as a party.

Section 3.  Tenant’s Covenants.  Tenant covenants and agrees: (a) to maintain all licenses and permits required for Tenant’s medical operations; (b) upon expiration or termination of this Lease, to remove its personal property and effects and to surrender the Leased Premises to Landlord in accordance with Article XVII;
and
(c) to comply with all applicable laws relating to Tenant’s specific use and occupancy of the Leased Premises, including applicable healthcare licensure and patient privacy laws

; and (d) Tenant’s use will not exceed the floor load, electrical, plumbing, water, or exhaust capacity allocated to the Leased Premises, and will not interfere with other tenants through vibration, odor, noise, or radiofrequency interference with adjacent diagnostic equipment.

all healthcare facility licenses, provider certifications, and other regulatory approvals required for Tenant’s operation of an outpatient medical facility at the Leased Premises, including any applicable state health department licensure and, if applicable, federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration.

all licenses, accreditations, certifications, permits, and registrations required for its operations, including applicable state facility licensure, DEA registration, CLIA certification, radiologic-materials licensing, and FDA-regulated device, drug, and biologic requirements. Failure to obtain or maintain any approval shall not constitute a Landlord default, abate rent, or create a termination right.

indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord from and against any third-party claims, losses, damages, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising from bodily injury, death, or property damage occurring within the Leased Premises, or arising from Tenant’s clinical operations, to the extent, and only to the extent, caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Tenant or its employees, agents, or contractors.

This indemnity shall not apply to the extent a final judgment determines that a claim was caused by Landlord’s negligence or willful misconduct, and it shall survive expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.
Section 2.  Subsequent Clinical Alterations.  Following the Initial Build-Out, Tenant may,

without Landlord’s consent but upon written notice to Landlord, install, modify, remove, and reconfigure examination rooms, treatment areas, privacy partitions, medical equipment, and related non-structural clinical improvements as Tenant’s outpatient service offerings evolve, provided
upon at least fifteen (15) business days’ prior written notice to Landlord, reconfigure movable partitions, casework, and finishes within the Leased Premises, provided
such work does not affect the structural components of the building or reduce the base building electrical capacity available to other tenants.

Any alteration affecting structural components, the building envelope, or systems shared with other tenants shall require Landlord’s consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and shall be deemed granted if Landlord fails to respond within ten (10) business days after receipt of Tenant’s complete plans and specifications.

Tenant shall confirm in writing that such work requires no permit, does not affect the building envelope, base-building systems, or fire- or life-safety systems, and does not reduce any base-building electrical, HVAC, plumbing, or exhaust capacity, and shall deliver as-built drawings to Landlord within thirty (30) days after completion. Any other alteration shall require Landlord’s prior written consent, which may be withheld in Landlord’s sole discretion.
